summary: Pamplona (about 205,000 people, per the draft; not re-checked) has eight municipal concession underground car parks (Plaza del Castillo, Plaza de Toros, Audiencia, Carlos III, Rincon de la Aduana, Blanca de Navarra, the hospital zone and the bus station) run by SABA, ACVIL, Aparcamiento San Roque, Gestion y Aparcamientos Pamplona, a Rincon de la Aduana operator, Empark (whose app brand is Telpark) and a bus-station joint venture. Council-approved tariffs rose 1.8% for 2025 and 2.7% for 2026 (in force from 1 January 2026), with 2026 daily maxima between 14.01 and 20.09 euro, and 48.02 euro at Plaza del Castillo on 6-15 July. On the street the council counted 34,307 regulated spaces in January 2026 (34,410 in its May 2026 award release), with 42,447 active resident and activity permits and 2,581 resident permits for 686 spaces in the Casco Antiguo. In May 2026 the regulated-parking and tow-truck contract was awarded to Dornier for 45.76 million euro over four years. A low emission zone covering the Casco Antiguo (not the Ensanches) was planned in the August 2025 draft ordinance for 1 January 2026, with penalties from 1 May 2026; a July 2026 press roundup reports fines of 200 euro, but no official confirmation of the sanctions start was found. Nine older park-and-ride lots with 2,464 spaces and free parking for 24 hours recorded 1.46 million entries in 2024; San Juan was announced as ready to open in June 2025, and for San Fermin 2026 the council announced that all park-and-ride lots would charge the orange-zone rate, with 1,117 operations recorded on 5-6 July. A 346-space underground car park in Calle Sangüesa was suspended in 2023, and the hospital had 1,290 open-air spaces in 2024 with 51 more rotation spaces contracted. A 2023 audit reported in regional press found all 4,681 resident spaces in the Casco Antiguo and Ensanche concession car parks occupied.

items.text: The eight municipal concession car parks (Plaza del Castillo, Plaza de Toros, Audiencia, Carlos III, Rincón de la Aduana, Blanca de Navarra, Zona Hospitalaria, Estación de Autobuses) raised tariffs 2.7% on 1 January 2026. The council checks and approves them each year. Listed daily maxima (VAT included) are 19.39 euro at Plaza del Castillo (48.02 euro on 6-15 July), 18.95 at Audiencia, 15.22 at Carlos III, 20.09 at Rincón de la Aduana and 14.01 at Plaza de Toros (10 hours or more).
items.source_title: Los ocho aparcamientos subterráneos actualizan sus tarifas y cánones para 2026 con un incremento del 2,7%

items.text: The hospital-zone car park has separate 2026 rotation tariffs for hospital workers (0.036 euro per minute for the first 15 minutes, 0.012 for minutes 121-600) and other users (0.060 and 0.020); monthly day season tickets cost 13.24 euro for staff and 53.00 euro for other users (VAT included).
items.source_title: Los ocho aparcamientos subterráneos actualizan sus tarifas y cánones para 2026 con un incremento del 2,7%

items.text: The eight municipal concession car parks (tariffs rose 1.8% for 2025) are run by SABA Aparcamientos (Plaza del Castillo), ACVIL Aparcamientos (Plaza de Toros), Aparcamiento San Roque (Audiencia), Gestion y Aparcamientos Pamplona (Carlos III), Parking Rincon de la Aduana (the December 2024 text calls it UTE Parkings de Pamplona, the January 2026 release names it without UTE), Empark Aparcamientos y Servicios (Blanca de Navarra and the hospital zone) and UTE Estacion de Autobuses de Pamplona (bus station). The council approved the 2025 update on 9 December 2024.
items.source_title: Las tarifas y cánones de los ocho aparcamientos subterráneos públicos de concesión administrativa se incrementan un 1,8%

items.text: On 27 January 2026 the council reported 34,307 regulated on-street spaces (18,710 orange, 13,230 blue), 127 more than assumed in the September 2025 tender, and 42,447 active resident and activity permits (41,290 resident cards, 1,072 activity cards). It also reported 3,066 spaces in a dozen park-and-ride lots. The Casco Antiguo has 2,581 resident permits for 686 spaces and the Ensanches 3,449 spaces. Compared with the tender figures, Iturrama has 254 fewer spaces and Rochapea 73 fewer, mainly after resurfacing and street works.
items.source_title: Pamplona cuenta con 34.307 plazas de aparcamiento regulado, 127 más de las contempladas en septiembre

items.text: Regulated parking runs Monday-Friday 08:30-14:00 and 16:00-20:00 and Saturday 08:30-14:00 (red zones from 09:00). Blue zone: vehicles with the sector's resident card park without time limit and others pay for the time ticketed; orange: ticket for a maximum of one day, with residents of the sector parking without a time limit. Tickets come from meters or the Telpark app. Exceptions include San Jorge (Renfe area) 24 hours a day. Page read on 21 October 2026.
items.source_title: Zonas de estacionamiento regulado (Ayuntamiento de Pamplona)

items.text: On 11 May 2026 the Junta de Gobierno Local awarded the regulated-parking and tow-truck contract to Dornier for 45.76 million euro over four years (headline: until 2030). It covers the blue zone, all park-and-ride lots, the motorhome lot and access control for the Casco Antiguo and low emission zone.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento de Pamplona destinará 45,8 millones de euros para la gestión del estacionamiento regulado y el servicio de grúa hasta el año 2030

items.text: On 27 August 2025 the Junta de Gobierno Local approved the draft ordinance for a low emission zone whose area coincides with the Casco Antiguo controlled-access zone. The draft was due to take effect on 1 January 2026, with a moratorium so that infringement and penalty provisions apply only from 1 May 2026. Residents, holders of garage spaces or shops in the zone, holders of the reduced-mobility card, loading and unloading, taxis and regular public transport are not subject to the environmental-badge restriction. The council forecast about 650 fewer vehicles a day (19.7%) and said the zone could be extended gradually to other districts by 2030. Final approval was still pending when the release was written.
items.source_title: Aprobado el proyecto de Ordenanza Reguladora de las Zonas de Bajas Emisiones

items.text: A July 2026 roundup lists Pamplona with Bilbao, San Sebastian and Vitoria-Gasteiz as cities already fining 200 euro for entering the low emission zone without a badge. It describes Pamplona's zone as the Casco Antiguo only, bounded by Taconera, Navas de Tolosa, Paseo de Sarasate, Duque de Ahumada, Juan de Labrit, Vergel and Huertas de Santo Domingo.
items.source_title: Radiografía de las zonas de bajas emisiones en Euskal Herria: dónde multan este verano

items.text: Nine free-for-24-hours park-and-ride lots with 2,464 spaces recorded 1,463,691 entries in 2024, up 21.8% on 2023, led by Mendebaldea (337,623 entries, average stay about 7 hours). Only 1.53% of entries stayed beyond the free 24 hours.
items.source_title: Más de 1.460.000 vehículos han accedido en 2024 a alguno de los nueve aparcamientos disuasorios

items.text: On 5 June 2025 the council announced that the San Juan park-and-ride (238 spaces plus 6 for reduced-mobility users) was ready to start operating within days, with licence-plate entry, 24 hours free and then 4.35 euro for the next 24 hours. San Juan, Lezkairu, Txantrea Sur and Ezkaba were adapted in the same 870,033-euro Next Generation EU works; San Juan was the first to open and the other three were expected to follow within weeks.
items.source_title: El aparcamiento disuasorio de San Juan, con cerca de 240 plazas de estacionamiento, listo para empezar a funcionar

items.text: The council announced on 19 June 2026, in the San Fermin municipal order (Bando) due to be signed in the following days, that practically the whole city except sector 1 would be an orange parking zone from 5 July to 14 July 2026. As a novelty, the park-and-ride lots would also charge the orange-zone rate, to avoid unregulated overnight stays and increase safety. The Casco Antiguo would be closed to traffic from 22:00 on 5 July to 14:00 on 15 July, and vehicle entry and exit at the bus-station and Baluarte car parks would be closed from 22:00 to 24:00 on festival days.
items.source_title: Todos los aparcamientos disuasorios de Pamplona pasarán a ser de pago del 5 al 14 de julio

items.text: On 5-6 July 2026, the first two days of paid parking in the twelve park-and-ride lots, the council counted 1,117 operations with an average stay of 284 minutes. It reported about 255,000 villavesa (urban bus) boardings on 6 July against 192,977 in 2025, when a strike limited service; the release gives the increase as 22.64%, but its own figures imply about 32%.
items.source_title: Normalidad en el primer día de las fiestas de San Fermín, con incremento en el uso del transporte urbano comarcal

items.text: In September 2024 the Hospital Universitario de Navarra had 1,290 open-air car spaces, 83 of them reserved for disabled users, plus 39 motorcycle spaces. On 16 September 2024 the council announced the award of a 204,558-euro contract (about three months of works) to create 51 regulated rotation spaces on a plot in front of Pabellon C, to give the haematology and oncology area rotation parking that eases access to consultations.
items.source_title: El Hospital Universitario de Navarra contará con 51 nuevas plazas de aparcamiento regulado tras la adecuación de un solar frente al Pabellón C

items.text: A council-commissioned audit of the city's 38 concession car parks, reported by regional press on 15 February 2023, found 13,944 spaces (10,665 resident-only, 3,279 rotation). It said all 4,681 resident spaces in the Casco Antiguo and Ensanche were occupied, with 1,001 people on waiting lists there and 448 for the hospital car park aimed at staff. The council cautioned that people may appear on several lists and that the lists are old, and the article also counted 585 free resident spaces elsewhere in the city. This is an older figure from a single regional press report; the audit itself was not seen.
items.source_title: El Casco Antiguo y Ensanche tienen ocupadas las 4.681 plazas de aparcamientos subterráneos municipales para residentes

items.text: In November 2023 the council described a proposed four-storey, 346-space underground car park in Calle Sangüesa. It was tendered together with the Plaza de la Cruz redevelopment as a single concession-and-works contract worth 13.7 million euro, of which the council would pay 2.58 million (for the plaza only) and the concessionaire 11.16 million, on a 75-year concession. Works began in July 2023 and were suspended less than a month later. A citizen consultation on both projects was announced for 11-17 December 2023.
items.source_title: La Casa de la Juventud acoge el lunes una sesión informativa sobre los proyectos de reurbanización de la plaza de la Cruz y de aparcamiento subterráneo en la calle Sangüesa

items.text: On 14 December 2023 the council suspended that consultation on the Calle Sangüesa car park and Plaza de la Cruz because of a no-confidence motion and no guarantee the result would be taken into account. No later status of the project was found.
items.source_title: Suspendida la consulta ciudadana en torno al aparcamiento subterráneo de la calle Sangüesa y la reurbanización de la Plaza de la Cruz

items.text: On 18 July 2025 the council announced that from 1 August 2025 electric vehicles left in a charging bay more than 15 minutes after charging ends would pay 0.20 euro per minute (maximum 50 euro), because charging bays in the city centre were being used as parking. At that date Pamplona had 29 publicly accessible charging stations with 65 charge points.
items.source_title: El Ayuntamiento de Pamplona cobrará a partir de agosto a los vehículos eléctricos que no se retiren de las plazas de los puntos de recarga

items.text: On 5 May 2026 the council and Telpark announced a free electric-vehicle charging campaign for 11-17 May 2026 in the Zona Hospitalaria, Baluarte and Blanca de Navarra underground car parks, using the Telpark app, with 25 semi-fast (up to 22 kW) and 4 fast (up to 60 kW) charge points. The release describes Telpark as concessionaire of regulated parking in Pamplona and as managing more than 2,400 spaces in these three car parks.
items.source_title: La semana del 11 al 17 de mayo se podrán recargar los vehículos eléctricos de forma gratuita en tres aparcamientos subterráneos de Pamplona
